Apple announced an expansion of its Supplier Employee Development Fund, a $50 million program for education support for supply chain workers, with the launch of a new Apple education center in Vietnam.

As Apple expands its production footprint beyond China, Vietnam is becoming an increasingly important manufacturing hub; the center operates in partnership with Hanoi University of Science and Technology (HUST)...

Apple first launched the Supplier Employee Development Fund in 2022 in response to concerns about the well-being of its supply chain workers. The company committed $50 million and said the program would combine worker education with respect for workers' rights.

The fund's previous work in Vietnam focused on training opportunities for people with disabilities, and this latest development appears to mirror an approach launched earlier this year in India.

Apple said the program has so far provided up to 9 million training sessions globally, with another 108,000 supply chain employees participating in a separate Swift coding course.
